Google just put $15B into Finland. Not for search. For AI.

On September 10, 2026, Google committed $15 billion to AI infrastructure in Finland — positioning compute near clean energy, favorable regulation, and subsea cable routes connecting multiple continents.

The same week, Qualcomm secured an AI chip deal with Amazon. Hyperscalers are actively diversifying their silicon supply chains. Nvidia still dominates at a $5.1 trillion market cap, but the hardware market is fragmenting by design.

This is the story most executives are missing. The AI race is no longer just about models. It is about where compute physically lives, who manufactures the chips, and which organizations locked in capacity before demand outstripped supply.

The infrastructure decisions being made this quarter have 3-5 year deployment horizons. The companies that align their AI strategy with the emerging geography of global compute will hold cost and latency advantages that compound year over year.
